idiom_name: GORM association auto-save (Create / FullSaveAssociations) in one transaction
implementation_notes: Go's database/sql has no mapping layer, so the work falls to an ORM: GORM's Create persists the association graph - addresses, collections, join rows - inside one transaction, and FullSaveAssociations on Updates forces a full-state write of the associated rows as well. That is the composite entity in Go form, but the update path is caller-driven: without FullSaveAssociations GORM updates only foreign-key references, so edits and removals inside a child collection are silently dropped. Teams that refuse GORM hand-write the mapper and run the child statements inside one db.Transaction.
pitfalls: Association Mode methods (Replace, Delete, Clear) touch foreign-key references only; the dependent rows survive unless Unscoped is used.
A Select/Omit that narrows Create quietly skips associations, so the composite is persisted partially while the call still returns no error.
Deleting with an empty primary key (Delete(&Order{})) cannot delete selected associations - GORM needs the zero-value-free key to build the condition.
